newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOs start week firm, but volume remains thin.
newsitem.headline: OLOs start week firm, but volume remains thin.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds started firm on Monday, boosted by reassuring messages from Luxmbourg, where European finance ministers said that EMU will start on time and that the Maastricht criteria will be respected.
OLO futures jumped to 121.93 in early trade but then fell back to 121.62, still 20 basis points higher. Traders said the move was exacerbated by the market's lack of liquidity.

Most primary dealers complained about the lack of investor interest in the market. "Either they are waiting to see what will happen with EMU, or they are unwilling to invest at these low yield levels," one dealer said.

One dealer expected OLOs to continue trending slightly higher, with the 10-year yield BE286= falling to 5.82 percent. It was at 5.85 percent from 5.88 percent late on Friday, offering a virtually unchanged nine bps over Bunds.

Some chartists pointed at the large head and shoulders formation that has been forming on the OLO and Bund futures weekly charts since the end of October, which could signal a major trend change if the formation were completed.
"The right shoulder is taking too long to my liking. But if support at 98.84 (on Bunds) is broken, the first target is at 94.00," said Bacob head of capital market trading Rudy Spaey.
He added that if Bund futures BDL: moved above 102.59 -- the top of the right side shoulder -- the formation would be broken, reducing the risk for a break of the long-term uptrend.
